LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 11.1.1 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS: INTERVIEWS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.1: Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Conversational Skills: interviews
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Conversational Skills: interviews, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to use polite language during an interview? 2. How do we show respect for others people’s opinion?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify polite words and expressions in a radio or television interview,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Conversational Skills: interviews in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use polite words and expressions when conducting an interview,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Conversational Skills: interviews in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the role of interviews in presenting reality. • Listen to a recorded or a role- played interview and identify polite expressions used. For example, “I am sorry but...”; “your point is valid, but...”, Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. • Watch a video in which the speakers are engaged in a radio or television interview, Learners with postural limitation could be preferentially positioned for enhanced viewing. • Make a list of the verbal and non-verbal cues used by the speakers to express politeness, 1. Why is it important to use polite language during an interview? 2. How do we show respect for others people’s opinion? 97 • In pairs, conduct an interview on choosing a career using polite expressions, • Search online and offline for typical questions and answers in a radio or television interview, Control light intensity for learners who are sensitive to light while using the digital devices. • Conduct a hot seating episode that relates to experiences people go through in their various careers.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Conversational Skills: interviews in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 11.1.1 Conversational Skills: interviews together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Collaboration is promoted as the learner observes the rules of engagement while playing different roles as interviewee or

interviewer.

• Digital literacy is enhanced as the learner uses both the radio and television as sources of information.

Values:
• Respect is developed as the learner disagrees politely while conducting the interview.

• Unity is promoted as the learner endeavours to achieve a common goal while organising and engaging in interviews with

peers.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Effective communication is achieved as the learner acquires skills for expressing opinions.

Link to other subjects:

Use of polite language is relevant to the concept of harmonious living in Religious Education and Social Studies.
